description: UTHMSPACE brings together students and educators from Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia. We combine engineering, Earth science, data analysis and web development to make NASA data easier to explore. Our Earth System Trend Detective connects climate, rainfall, ocean conditions and solar resources through interactive maps, statistics and forecasting. With interests in AI and satellite propagation, we value teamwork, clear visualisation and transparent scientific interpretation.
summary: Earth System Trend Detective helps students and communities investigate what is changing, where it is changing, and how strong the evidence is. Built by UTHMSPACE, it turns NASA POWER records into location comparisons, trend estimates and worldwide maps. A hotspot explorer highlights relatively strong warming and drying candidates. Connected demonstrations use 20 years of Giovanni/GPM IMERG monthly rainfall, paired MODIS Aqua sea-surface temperature and chlorophyll, NASA GEOS-CF air-quality forecasts, and solar-resource scenarios. A working machine-learning forecast reports test performance and uncertainty; an engineering extension estimates satellite and terrestrial rain attenuation using separate ITU-R climatology and propagation models. Source labels, units, missing-data rules and downloadable evidence make the investigations traceable. We clearly distinguish observed environmental products, model estimates and artificial fish illustrations. This educational prototype supports exploration rather than operational warnings; limited ocean coverage, forecast uncertainty and engineering assumptions remain visible.
details:
THE QUESTION AND OUR SOLUTION

Environmental trends can move in different directions in different places. A useful investigation connects the variable, location, time period, rate of change and strength of evidence. UTHMSPACE developed Earth System Trend Detective for the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge.

Our workflow is:

  1. choose a variable and location
  2. inspect its time series
  3. compare a second location
  4. explore the worldwide pattern
  5. export the evidence.

NASA POWER supplies temperature at 2 m, corrected precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed and surface solar energy. These satellite-informed and model/reanalysis products are not individual weather-station measurements.

NASA DATA, LOCAL EVIDENCE AND GLOBAL CONTEXT

Historical analysis retrieves monthly POWER records, preserves missing observations, requires complete years for annual summaries and aligns common complete years for two-location comparisons. Rainfall rates are converted using actual calendar-month durations when accumulated totals are required. The app reports OLS trends, Sen slopes with 95% intervals and a preliminary Mann–Kendall/Kendall trend test.

A live 2005–2024 comparison retained 20 complete years for Johor Bahru and London. Their Sen temperature slopes were approximately +0.038 and +0.044 °C/year. Johor’s interval was +0.016 to +0.059 °C/year, with p ≈ 0.0024; London’s interval crossed zero, with p ≈ 0.0548. This demonstrates why trend magnitude and uncertainty should be examined together. The difference between the slopes is descriptive; no formal between-location test is performed.

Worldwide maps show annual/monthly values, and the 2005–2024 period means and Sen slopes are prepared. The Hotspots view screens warming, drying or their intersection using area-weighted thresholds and connected candidate areas. A live global warming run screened 207,936 eligible cells and found 25,569 candidate cells in 194 connected areas at the strongest 10% area threshold. Candidates depend on the study rectangle and include oceans under the selected mask. They are not validated hazard zones or statistical-significance clusters.

KEY FEATURES AND ENGINEERING APPLICATIONS

A. RAINFALL AND ENGINEERING APPLICATION

The rainfall investigation distinguishes POWER PRECTOTCORR, based on bias-corrected MERRA-2, from GPM IMERG Final Run V07 satellite–gauge precipitation estimates. Its genuine Giovanni demonstration contains 240 monthly observations for January 2005–December 2024 over 102–104°E, 1–3°N. One-click loading provides rainfall totals, climatology, monthly empirical CCDFs and provenance. Independent arithmetic confirmed that 1 of 240 months exceeded 500 mm, or 0.4167%; the January subset contained 20 observations, and none exceeded 500 mm.

A monthly CCDF describes the fraction of months above a monthly depth threshold. It is not annual one-minute rainfall exceedance, R0.01 or communication-link availability. The fixed rectangle includes land and sea and is not Johor’s administrative boundary. Other IMERG locations and periods need reviewed imports; automatic arbitrary-region retrieval is not connected.

The working rain-attenuation extension uses separate ITU-R source climatology and rain-only propagation models: P.837-8, P.839-4, P.838-3, P.618-14 for satellite links, and P.530-19 for terrestrial reference links. Supplied scientific grids undergo checksum and structural validation. Users set the scenario, calculate contour maps, inspect point results and percentage-exceedance curves, and export calculated evidence.

A live satellite scenario at 20 GHz, horizontal polarization, 30° elevation and p = 0.01% produced 289 valid grid nodes and 544 filled contour pieces over the 102–104°E, 1–3°N rectangle. At 2°N, 103°E, estimated rain attenuation was 53.0846 dB. These are long-term scenario estimates, not observed outages or a full link budget. Monthly NASA rainfall is not converted into the ITU one-minute input. However, such a database could be utilised to convert to shorter intervals, such as one-minute CCDF statistics, for predicting rain attenuation.

B. FISHERIES ENVIRONMENT

The updated fisheries demonstration combines real January 2024 MODIS Aqua SST, processing R2019.0, and chlorophyll-a, R2022.0.3, in two labelled maps. Native nominal 9 km data are aggregated to 1° area-weighted global overviews with land, missing-data and coverage rules. Prepared sample histories retain native-grid support.

Fish icons are explicitly labelled artificial illustrations and can be hidden. No fish observations, population model, catch forecast or validated habitat-suitability model is supplied. Only one month is installed, so the current ocean demonstration cannot establish warming or chlorophyll trends. Additional years are necessary for a temporal investigation.

C. FORECASTS, AIR QUALITY AND SOLAR ENERGY

The live Python/scikit-learn forecast selected gradient-boosted trees for a Johor temperature demonstration trained through December 2024. On 72 test errors, MAE was 0.521 °C versus a 0.567 °C baseline, an 8.1% improvement. The nominal 95% intervals covered 83.3% of test outcomes, showing uncertainty remains imperfect. Its January–March 2025 outputs are retrospective relative to that training cutoff, not present-day weather forecasts. Temporal dependence, distribution shift, small holdouts and hosted-service availability remain limitations.

The GEOS-CF extension successfully returned 72 of 72 requested forecast hours. It displays modelled PM2.5 and estimated PM2.5 AQI with timestamps and exports. This is not a monitoring-station observation, a full multi-pollutant AQI or Malaysia’s official API/IPU. Local validation and forecast intervals are unavailable.

PV Energy Yield applies capacity × irradiation × duration × assumed performance ratio to POWER solar data. A 5 kWp, 80% performance-ratio Johor scenario estimated 6,582.3 kWh for 2024. It is a horizontal-system scenario; tilt, shading, thermal behaviour, inverter losses and measured-plant validation require further work.

INNOVATION, USABILITY AND POTENTIAL IMPACT

Our contribution is a traceable investigation experience connecting local questions, statistical evidence, worldwide context and application scenarios. Presets, coordinate/place selection, A/B comparison, readable legends, quality labels, one-click demonstrations and CSV/JSON exports make NASA products easier to question and explain. Prepared, checksum-verified layers reduce repeated dependence on upstream downloads.

The intended users are students, educators and exploratory community planners. Working investigations demonstrate educational value and technical feasibility. Adoption, improved decisions and economic or environmental benefits have not yet been measured.

TECHNICAL EXECUTION AND CURRENT LIMITS

The app uses React/TypeScript, TanStack, Tailwind, Google Maps/Places, Leaflet/OpenStreetMap and Recharts, with scientific preparation and modelling in TypeScript and Python. Work records contain reference tests for units, missing data, calendar durations, common-year alignment, source integrity and propagation calculations. Selected numerical reference cases and independent CCDF arithmetic were checked during review; the full repository test suite was not independently rerun.

Point significance tests are preliminary: temporal dependence, multiple testing and causal attribution need further assessment. Spatial/hotspot results are descriptive. Grid cells are not political boundaries or local gauges; zooming adds no measurement resolution. Attenuation is rain-only and does not model actual terrestrial endpoints, terrain, obstructions or complete availability. One known terrestrial metadata issue retains the satellite elevation in the displayed/exported inclination; the attenuation calculation derives the correct inclination from the antenna geometry. This requires correction before relying on that metadata.

SI USE AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS

ChatGPT and Lovable assisted ideation, research, interface design, coding/debugging, data preparation and writing. The forecast uses an identified ML model; artificial fish symbols are distinguished from scientific observations. NASA supplies the cited environmental products; ITU-R supplies the separate propagation references. Google Maps/OpenStreetMap provide location and basemap services. The team remains responsible for reviewing assumptions, credits and final content.
